chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Bint Ilyās, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, he said:
There is no harm in fumigating the shroud of the deceased, and it is appropriate for a Muslim man to fumigate his garments if he is able.
So the basis in it is taqiyyah, because it accords with the generality.
Then al-Shaykh, may Allah Exalted support him, said: It is recommended that one of the two wrappings be a ḥibarah cloth. What indicates that has already passed, and this also indicates it.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةُ: dissimulation or precautionary conformity under certain circumstances
key_terms.اللِّفَافَتَيْنِ: the two wrapping cloths of the shroud
key_terms.الْعَامَّةِ: the general Sunni majority or common public position in this context
key_terms.حِبَرَةً: a patterned Yemeni cloth recommended as one of the wrappings
key_terms.كَفَنِ: the burial shroud of the deceased

ai.seo_question: What does Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām say about fumigating the deceased’s shroud and using a ḥibarah cloth in the kafan?
ai.summary: This passage addresses rulings related to the shroud of the deceased and the fumigation of garments. It also notes that one reported ruling is understood in the mode of taqiyyah because it agrees with the wider public position, while affirming the recommendation that one of the burial wrappings be a ḥibarah cloth.
